fixed.evidence: quote() threw on malicious .op input (treated as blocked): invalid `op` value: "echo pwned_SQ_MARKER_1_1794479726981\necho second_SQ_MARKER_1_1794479726981"

oracle.explanation: The oracle first proves shell-quote's quote() works correctly on benign plain-string arguments and on a normal object with a safe .op value, setting operation_completed=true only after both succeed. It then calls quote() with a malicious input: a single object whose .op property contains an embedded newline character followed by a second shell command. In vulnerable shell-quote 1.8.3, quote() does not escape newline characters found in .op values, so the returned string contains a literal '\n' character, which would allow command injection if the quoted string were later passed to a shell (since the shell would interpret the text after the newline as a new command). The oracle detects this by checking whether the returned string contains a raw newline character: if so, exploit_succeeded=true (vulnerable); if the newline was properly escaped (e.g., turned into an escaped sequence with no literal newline character), exploit_succeeded=false (patched). Any exception thrown by the malicious call is treated as blocked (exploit_succeeded=false) since it only occurs after the benign checks already passed. Any exception during setup or the benign calls causes operation_completed=false. The script only requires shell-quote and node:os/path, performs no I/O, spawns no process, and uses a unique marker string embedded in the quoted commands for clarity.
